item.title: RPAx Instabilities from Ground- and Excited-State References
item.description: arXiv:2610.36154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random-phase approximation with exchange (RPAx) calculations based on ground- or excited-state references can yield complex excitation energies, causing the corresponding RPAx correlation energy to become complex as well. In this work, we investigate the origin of these complex energies using \ce{H2} in the 6-31G basis set as a minimal model. For the ground-state restricted Hartree-Fock reference, complex roots emerge at the well-known triplet instability associated with the appearance of a lower-lying unrestricted, symmetry-broken solution. For excited-state references, we identify two distinct mechanisms leading to complex excitation energies. The first is similarly associated with symmetry breaking. The second arises when a positive-energy excitation becomes degenerate with the positive-energy de-excitation associated with a negative-energy transition. Finally, we demonstrate the practical implications of these findings for spin-flip Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations of cyclobutadiene and state-specific core-ionization calculations for selected systems. These examples show that, in the absence of the relevant instabilities, methods sharing the generalized eigenvalue structure of RPAx can be applied to excited-state references without resorting to the Tamm-Dancoff or core-valence separation approximations, while retaining real excitation energies.
item.dc:creator: Loris Burth, Marios-Petros Kitsaras, Pierre-Fran\c{c}ois Loos

item.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. I. Molecular dissociation with fixed real-space and orbital partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.36514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Van Aggelen et al. [Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 11, 5558 (2009)] showed that variational second-order reduced-density-matrix (2-RDM) calculations with the standard two-index conditions dissociate diatomic molecules into fractionally charged atoms with energies far below the exact limit, a drastic violation of size consistency; the proposed subsystem constraints require auxiliary calculations with the physical fragment Hamiltonians. We show that two long-known ingredients, combined, remove most of this failure without such calculations: the requirement that the number of electrons in a part of the molecule be an integer, imposed as linear conditions on the 2-RDM, and a chemically motivated partition of the molecule into atomic regions bounded at the bond critical point of the Hartree-Fock density. In a minimal basis, compared with full configuration interaction, a single such condition reduces the energy errors of NO$^+$ and CN$^-$ at 6 {\AA} from 108.9 and 80.7 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ to less than 0.02 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. In N$_2^+$, whose fragments have the correct mean population but too small a fluctuation, the region and three-index conditions act complementarily, reducing the error at 4 {\AA} from 138.0 to 1.6 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. At the separated-atom limit, the region cuts make the $P$, $Q$, $G$ energy additive over the fragments to within 0.2 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ in 7 of 10 systems, 3 already nearly additive without cuts; adding the $T_1$ and $T_2$ conditions also makes CO nearly additive, while a nonadditive error remains for N$_2^+$ and CO$^+$. Effective partitions are those whose condition is nearly saturated by the exact state.
item.dc:creator: Maho Nakata

item.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.36839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO$_2$ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Yu Zhou, Wentao Zhang, Mouyi Weng, Zhao-Yi Yan, Lin-Wang Wang

item.title: Multireference Second-Order Perturbation Theories Based on Iterative Configuration Interaction with Selection
item.description: arXiv:2610.37221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under the assumption that the static correlation can well be described by selected configuration interaction, to the extent that the residual dynamic correlation can be accounted for accurately by a second-order perturbation theory (PT2), a family of multireference PT2s (iCI-MRPT2) based on the iterative configuration interaction with selection are proposed and compared. The first step is to partition a large complete active space (CAS) $P$ into the direct sum of a primary ($P_m$) and a secondary ($P_s$) subspace via a parameter $C_{\mathrm{min}}$. The former serves as the actual reference space, whereas the latter is treated via Epstein-Nesbet PT2. An MRPT2 is then invoked to account for the dynamic correction of the $Q=1-P$ space to the $P_m$ space. Different MRPT2s are distinguished by the underlying zeroth-order Hamiltonians. To circumvent the prohibitive computational cost and memory footprint associated with high-order reduced density matrices in the fully internally contracted scheme and the exponential growth of external functions (XF) in the uncontracted scheme, a partial contraction strategy is employed for constructing the XFs: those involving one or two inactive (core or virtual) orbitals are kept uncontracted, whereas those involving three or four inactive orbitals are internally contracted. They span the uncontracted ($Q_u$) and contracted ($Q_c$) portions of $Q$, respectively. The former is further split into two subspaces $Q_u^c$ and $Q_u^u$ via a parameter $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$, which are to be treated in coupled and uncoupled manners, respectively. Extrapolations to zero $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{min}}$ can be performed, so as to approach CAS-based MRPT2. Calculations with active spaces as large as CAS(56e,58o) can now be performed. The size-consistency of the iCI-MRPT2s is also analyzed in detail.
item.dc:creator: Ning Zhang, Wenjian Liu

item.title: StudDFT: A quantum chemistry program for educational and research purposes
item.description: arXiv:2610.37483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: StudDFT is a quantum chemistry program for Hartree--Fock (HF), density functional theory (DFT), and second-order M{\o}ller--Plesset (MP2) calculations of small and medium-sized molecules. It is intended primarily for teaching and student research, but its accuracy suffices for routine research calculations. Version 1.30.2 implements the RHF/UHF, RKS/UKS, and RMP2/UMP2/PUMP2 schemes in Gaussian basis sets, including effective core potentials (ECP); LDA, GGA (BLYP, BP86, BPW91, PBE), meta-GGA (r$^2$SCAN), global hybrid (B3LYP, PBE0) and range-separated hybrid ($\omega$B97, $\omega$B97X, $\omega$B97X-D) functionals; analytical gradients and Hessians; geometry optimization, transition-state and reaction-path (IRC) searches, potential energy surface scans, harmonic frequencies and IR intensities, thermochemistry, counterpoise corrections, D3(BJ) dispersion, polarizable continuum solvation, density fitting (RI-J/RI-JK), linear-response TDDFT, and fractional-occupation smearing. The program has been verified against ORCA and PySCF on 50 molecules (30 for optimizations): the mean absolute deviations of the single-point energies do not exceed 7 $\mu$Ha for HF, MP2, and the LDA, GGA, and global hybrid functionals except PBE and PBE0, whose systematic shifts of several tens of $\mu$Ha are traced mainly to the value of $\mu$ in the PBE exchange; those of the optimized interatomic distances and harmonic frequencies do not exceed 1.2$\times$10$^{-4}$ {\AA} and 1.2 cm$^{-1}$. Corrections made since the first public version (0.82), mainly affecting vibrational frequencies, are documented with their effect on the verification results. Unlike large multi-language packages, StudDFT is a monolithic Fortran code with OpenMP parallelization, which simplifies its use in courses. Binaries for Windows and Linux, the documentation, and all test inputs and outputs are freely available.
item.dc:creator: Stanislav K. Ignatov

item.title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
item.description: arXiv:2610.36286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}\Sigma_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.
item.dc:creator: Leonid V. Skripnikov, Michail Athanasakis-Kaklamanakis, Carlos M. Fajardo-Zambrano

item.title: Where Does the Anion-Redox Hole Go? Reliability of Open-Shell Projection-Based Embedding for Li-Rich Cathodes, from DFT Environments to Quantum Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2610.36659v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anion redox in Li-rich layered oxides places holes on oxygen next to an antiferromagnetic Mn(IV) d3 lattice, a strongly correlated open-shell problem for which projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding offers a route to correlated and quantum solvers, but whose errors are known mainly for closed-shell molecules. We develop a spin-unrestricted projection-based embedding, exact at the DFT-in-DFT level to the microhartree scale for closed-shell, broken-symmetry and high-spin references with point charges, and apply DMRG-in-DFT to point-charge clusters of delithiated Li(2-x)MnO3, varying the environment functional (0-100% exact exchange), geometry, active region, active-space spin, virtual space, cluster size and magnetic reference. In every setting the lowest SCF state places the hole on an oxygen pair, with no O-O bond. How the hole is shared depends on the functional together with the geometry: hybrids give a full, uncoupled hole at the DFT+U geometry but a partial, weakly covalent hole at their own geometry, a change of up to 0.5 e on one oxygen. Where spin spreads across the active/environment boundary, the integer spin projection of the active space becomes a choice worth up to 0.26 e, and at most 0.09 e once the two Mn neighbors are included. An extended state search found missed lower states for two functionals, changing a pair-oxygen spin by up to 0.45 e. Across all 82 runs the embedded mean field gives the same hole (median DMRG change 0.02-0.04 e); correlation mainly adds O-O covalency. State control and geometry consistency, not the solver, dominate the uncertainty, and total energies are not converged at 30-40 orbitals. For quantum solvers, the embedded Hamiltonian must be spin-unrestricted: a shared-orbital form reverses the hole, while sample-based quantum diagonalization reproduces exact diagonalization, as accurately as, but not better than, classical selected CI.
item.dc:creator: Pritam Das, Satadeep Bhattacharjee, Pil-Ryung Cha

item.title: On-the-fly Estimation of Quantum-Corrected Thermodynamics in LAMMPS
item.description: arXiv:2610.37586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a native implementation of the Two/Three-Phase Thermodynamics (xPT, $x \in \{2,3\}$) method within the LAMMPS molecular dynamics framework, termed FixXPT. xPT is an approach for obtaining absolute, quantum-corrected thermodynamics (entropy, enthalpy, free energy, heat capacity, diffusivity) from the density of states function, obtained from the velocity autocorrelation function of an equilibrium trajectory. FixXPT addresses non-trivial integration challenges, including atom reordering, compute scheduling, FFT backends, unit systems, and partitioning of atomic velocities into molecular modes. Two autocorrelators are provided: a Wiener-Khinchin FFT correlator with one cumulative window-end operation, and an in-line multi-tau correlator whose memory footprint grows only logarithmically with the window length, removing the principal scaling bottleneck for long analysis windows. The velocity history of each window is distributed across the MPI ranks, so the memory the fix adds to a node stays nearly constant as ranks are added and its cost falls with the number of GPUs. Replaying identical velocity frames through FixXPT and the stand-alone pyxPT post-processor reproduces every thermodynamic observable of well-sampled groups to within 0.1 to 0.5% across the full analysis-mode matrix; sparsely populated ionic species agree within their statistical uncertainty, and the multi-tau VACF converges monotonically to the FFT result as its buffer grows, from 0.8% to 0.1% drift across a 16-fold buffer sweep. The code is distributed as a drop-in LAMMPS package.
item.dc:creator: Robert Ramji, Ilya Mazalov, Ricardo Buarque, Alexandria Do, Xiaoxu Ruan, Tod A. Pascal

item.title: Rotational-state-controlled dissociative ionization dynamics in $\mathrm{CF_2I_2}$
item.description: arXiv:2608.04715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigated strong-field dissociative ionization of $\mathrm{CF_2I_2}$ ensembles prepared in different initial rotational-state distributions using an electrostatic deflector. Pronounced changes in ion-channel branching ratios revealed a strong dependence of the fragmentation dynamics on the initial rotational excitation. Analysis of fragment yields and their laser-power dependences identifies resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization through an intermediate excited state, $\mathrm{CF_2I_2^{\ast}}$. The measured branching behavior indicates competition between stabilization into bound ionic states and dissociative channels, driven by near-threshold non-adiabatic Coriolis-type coupling. Tuning the rotational energy by only a few $\mu$eV is sufficient to significantly alter the ionization dynamics and to redistribute the reaction products. These findings demonstrate the key role of rotational excitation in controlling non-adiabatic dynamics following strong-field ionization of $\mathrm{CF_2I_2}$.
item.dc:creator: Nidin Vadassery, Ivo S. Vinkl\'arek, Sebastian Trippel, Jochen K\"upper

item.title: Human Language Shapes the Emerging Physical Reasoning in Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.20666v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Whether large language models (LLMs) acquire adequate representations of physical reality by predicting the next token remains unresolved. Molecular conformations provide a quantitative test: we asked 28 LLMs to rank 810 geometries of 27 molecules from atomic coordinates alone. Frontier LLMs approach the accuracy of specialized force fields, but their ability is bound to well-defined chemical concepts. They rank conformers with more hydrogen bonds as more stable, inverting the true order when the hydrogen-bonded conformer is less stable. On pairs with equal hydrogen-bond counts, they are most accurate for molecules whose explanations invoke hydrogen bonding, whereas molecules governed by ring strain remain difficult. Thus, the physical understanding emerging in LLMs inherits the structure and blind spots of human scientific discourse, a machine analogue of linguistic relativity.
item.dc:creator: Gregorii A. Semakin, Timofey V. Losev, Ilya V. Prolomov, Stepan N. Ostarkov, Igor V. Alabugin, Michael G. Medvedev
